domain: EU law enforcement / infringement procedures against Member States (case-level escalation)
prediction_question: For an open European Commission infringement case against a Member State at a decision instant (e.g. the date a letter of formal notice is decided), will the case escalate to the next procedural stage (reasoned opinion, then referral to the Court of Justice) or be closed without escalation within a stated horizon?
prediction_time: The publication instant of the Commission's monthly infringement package / the register entry for the decision in question (to be pinned against the register's actual channel; the monthly packages are dated presscorner publications). Features would be the case's stage reached, policy area, topic, Member State, case age and the case's decision history - all published register fields; the future decisions are the label and must be excluded.
target_definition: Binary label derived from the case's decision history in the register: escalation to the next stage (or a named later stage) vs closure without escalation, within a stated horizon after the instant. Label source = later decision entries for the same case number (INFR(YYYY)NNNN), excludable from features.

sources.name: European Commission infringement register / 'Implementing EU law' site (interactive maps, graphs and per-case register search by decision, status, type, Member State, policy area)
sources.api_cases: https://ec.europa.eu/implementing-eu-law/search-infringement-decisions/api/infringements (POST JSON, paged, one record per case with the full decisions[] history embedded)
sources.access: RESOLVED 2026-10-31 (was the recorded blocker): the register application is backed by an anonymous, unauthenticated JSON API captured from the publisher's own web app (no login, no key). /api/decisions returns per-decision rows (62,957 total) with fields activeInfringementCase, caseType, decisionDate, decisionType, infringementNumber, leadDg, memberState, memo(+URL), nonCommunicationCase, normalCuriaReference(+URL), policyAreas[], pressRelease(+URL), title. /api/infringements returns one record per case (25,838 total) with the same case fields plus decisions[] carrying the complete dated decision history per case - the per-case panel is available directly from the publisher. The app also exposes 'Export Search Url' / 'Export to Excel' controls (page text observed 2026-10-31). Date filters accept DD/MM/YYYY only (YYYY-MM-DD returns HTTP 500); decisionCategory accepts the referencedata keys (LFN, RO, RTC, CLOSURES, ALFN, ARO, ...). The 2026-10-28 URL spellings with _en now return HTTP 500; the current paths use /en. The monthly infringement packages remain PDFs on the presscorner (e.g. INF_25_2077 of 2025-10-08, INF_26_431 of 2026-03); the third-party scraping API (brubru.beresol.eu) remains irrelevant.

measurements.publisher_cross_check: 2023 Annual Report on monitoring the application of EU law (commission.europa.eu, read 2026-10-31): Commission closed 1,038 infringement cases in 2023 (680 after LFN, 300 after RO, 20 post-referral pre-application, 25 after Art. 258 judgment, 13 withdrawn from Court) and referred 82 cases to the CJEU. Measured API 2023 category counts are consistent in scale: CLOSURES 1,037 vs reported 1,038 closed; RTC 37 decisions in-year vs 82 referrals decided (referral decisions land in later years); LFN 528; RO 267.
measurements.fetch_cost_measured: Bounded probe 2026-10-31: ~135 small POST/GET requests (1-3 rows each, <=4 KB responses), ~3 min wall clock on the coordinator. Full fetch ARITHMETIC (estimate, not measured): decisions endpoint 62,957 rows at size=200 -> ~315 requests; cases endpoint 25,838 cases at size=200 -> ~130 requests; each measured page <=~200 KB, so a full case-level panel is plausibly ~25-50 MB in ~130 requests - a worker-sized fetch, never attempted because the lead closed.
measurements.timing_observation: Register updated in real time per the publisher's 2023 annual report ('The Commission's public register of infringement cases... is updated in real time'); decisions are announced in dated monthly infringement packages on the presscorner (e.g. INF_25_2077 of 2025-10-08, INF_26_431 of 2026-03). Decision rows carry the publisher's own decision dates; the register is a living database, so any historical vintage question would have needed an as-of policy recorded before construction (mooted by the drop).

rejection_reason: Mirror with the precedent named. The access blocker recorded on 2026-10-28 is RESOLVED (the register is backed by a public anonymous JSON API with a case-level endpoint embedding full decision histories), and the licence is class A - but the natural task family on this source is already published. The candidate's primary label - will a case at the formal-notice stage escalate to a reasoned opinion, vs close without escalation - is posed, on this exact register, by a 2026 peer-reviewed study (tandfonline 10.1080/13501763.2026.2739423, ~19,600 unique cases 2002-2020, 'assign the value (1) if we observe the issuing of a Reasoned Opinion and (0) only if the case was closed without a prior Reasoned Opinion', escalation base rate ~34%), whose assembled case-level replication dataset is publicly released, CC0 and unrestricted (Harvard Dataverse doi:10.7910/DVN/LGADVE, replication_PP.zip 71,421,134 bytes, versionState RELEASED, verified 2026-10-31 via the Dataverse API). A consumer can already download the task's data with the exact label. The adjacent formulations are also covered: stage histories through referral to the CJEU and to judgment (Boerzel & Knoll infringement database 1978-1999, public download; Fjelstul & Carrubba stage-history models), duration-to-outcome and Art. 260 compliance/sanctions (compliance literature). What would remain ours - refreshed years 2021-2026, chronological splits, a corrected censoring rule for the active cases, fixtures - is packaging of someone else's formulation, not a genuinely novel task. Under the operator's standing bar we ship nothing rather than mirror. Initiation targets are impossible from this register by design (it records only initiated procedures, as the 2026 paper notes).
review: 2026-10-31: the recorded next probe ran exactly as specified (browser inspection of the register application). It found a public anonymous JSON API (decisions + case-level endpoints) and a class A licence - the two facts that would have made this candidate buildable - and the novelty sweep then found the task already published with a public CC0 replication dataset, which is decisive against publication under the standing bar. The drop is a novelty drop, NOT an access or licence drop: any reopen must bring a genuinely different target variable with its own recorded novelty sweep; the measured access/licence/population evidence in this record stands and need not be re-probed.
next_action: Closed for the procedural-escalation family on this register (LFN->RO, RO->CJEU referral, Art. 260 post-judgment, duration-to-closure) - all covered by named published prior art, and the primary label's assembled dataset is already publicly downloadable (CC0). Reopen only with (a) a task contract on this register whose target variable is genuinely different from the published family, with its own recorded novelty sweep naming the new prior art, and (b) reuse of this record's measured channel/licence/population evidence - do not re-probe the API or re-read the licence. Do not reopen merely to refresh the 2002-2020 replication data to 2026 or to add splits/censoring corrections to it - that is a repackage of a shipped task.

Attribution 'European Commission - infringement decisions register'; conditions carried into any derived work. The class stands even though the candidate is dropped on novelty: it is the measured licence posture of this source.
uncertainty: None material. The one measurement never made - per-case stage-transition base rates on a full panel - cannot change the verdict: the published replication dataset already contains the assembled case-level data with the primary label, so measuring our own base rates would only re-measure their published ~34% escalation rate. If a genuinely different target is ever proposed (see next_action reopen hook), the per-case panel can be fetched with the documented API in ~130 requests (cases endpoint) and the split counts then computed on the worker.

prior_art: Tandfonline 10.1080/13501763.2026.2739423 (2026) + its CC0 replication dataset doi:10.7910/DVN/LGADVE; Boerzel & Knoll 2012 infringement-db.jmce.org; Fjelstul & Carrubba 2018
novelty_check.theirs: Hagedorn/Marx/Thijs et al-type officials-bias study (JEPP/JEUR 'National, partisan or ideological biases? How EU officials characteristics can influence infringement proceeding outcomes', tandfonline 10.1080/13501763.2026.2739423): exact LFN->RO escalation variable on all register decisions 2002-2020, ~19,600 cases, base rate ~34%; replication dataset released CC0, unrestricted, on Harvard Dataverse (doi:10.7910/DVN/LGADVE, replication_PP.zip 71.4 MB, versionState RELEASED, verified 2026-10-31). Older: Boerzel/Knoll infringement database 1978-1999 (public download, stage histories to ECJ judgment); Fjelstul/Carrubba stage-history models incl. referrals; duration/compliance (Art. 260) literature.
novelty_check.ours: Nothing publishable on the natural target: the procedural-escalation family (formal notice -> reasoned opinion -> referral to CJEU -> Art. 260) on this exact register is already published. A 2026 peer-reviewed paper poses precisely the candidate's primary label (RO issued after a formal notice, 1/0, ~19,600 cases 2002-2020, censored active cases counted as 0) on the Commission's own infringement database, and ships the assembled case-level dataset publicly. Stage-2 referral, duration and Art. 260 compliance variants are covered by the older political-science literature (stage-history models; 1978-1999 infringement database). Remaining 'ours' would be freshness to 2026, chronological splits and corrected censoring - packaging, not a new task; under the standing bar we ship nothing rather than mirror.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
